title: Lesson 8: Middleware Tradeoffs: MuleSoft vs Boomi vs Custom (and When Salesforce Is the Hub)
description: How to choose the integration layer: MuleSoft's API-led pro-code platform, Boomi's low-code iPaaS, hand-rolled custom code, and the decision matrix for when Salesforce itself should be the hub instead of any middleware at all.

questions.question: Why does a middleware hub beat point-to-point wiring as systems multiply?
options: Pairwise connections grow with the square of the system count; a hub grows linearly.
Point-to-point wiring is always faster to build and far cheaper to maintain over time.
A hub removes the need for any authentication between connected systems.
Point-to-point connections stop working once three systems exist.
questions.explanation: Every pair of systems needs its own connection, so point-to-point count grows with the square of systems while a hub needs each system to connect only once.

questions.question: Under the orchestration test, when does an integration genuinely need middleware?
options: When it makes one synchronous call to a single system and returns a value.
When it only needs to schedule a nightly bulk transfer between two systems.
When it needs complex flow logic, aggregation, transformation, or transactional integrity.
When it must display live external data inside the org without ever copying it into local storage.
questions.explanation: Middleware earns its cost only for real orchestration: complex flow logic, aggregation across systems, transformation, or transactional integrity that spans systems.

questions.question: Why is the true cost of a custom integration higher than its build cost suggests?
options: Custom code always requires a recurring per-user software license.
Most of the total cost is maintenance spread over years.
Custom integrations cannot be monitored or tested in any way.
The build cost is fixed while maintenance turns out to be free.
questions.explanation: Development is only a fraction of a custom integration's cost, because updates, API changes, retesting, and adaptations consume most of the total over its life.
